comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom discuss significant restructuring and other charges in Item 7. Intel's disclosure focuses on the specific components of its 2023 results, including a $1.2 billion benefit from VLSI litigation, a $401 million EC fine, and a $353 million termination fee for the failed Tower Semiconductor acquisition. Broadcom provides a similar high-level overview of its fiscal year charges, noting $1,533 million in 2024 primarily due to VMware-related cost reductions and $244 million in 2023 primarily related to IP litigation. While Intel highlights litigation outcomes and acquisition terminations as key charge drivers, Broadcom highlights merger-related restructuring costs, showing different operational challenges but the same category of non-recurring financial impacts.
